name: CO-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+20 partisan lean makes the seat structurally Democratic
Neguse has $3.1M on hand while his challenger reports no fundraising
No polls or expert ratings; a low-profile race
model.rationale: The district's twenty-point Democratic lean, Neguse's roughly $3 million financial advantage over an essentially unfunded Republican challenger, and markets pricing his win odds near 98% all point to a safe hold; the weak challenger justifies a slight nudge above the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: A last-minute infusion of outside spending for the challenger could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat itself remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Colorado's second district sits firmly in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty points toward the party. Joe Neguse, seeking another term, enters the general election with about $3.1 million on hand after raising $2.7 million, while Republican Kelley Dennison reports no measurable fundraising and Libertarian Gaylon Kent also appears on the ballot. Prediction markets price Neguse's chances near 98 percent.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Democratic fundamentals, Neguse's incumbency advantage, and the lopsided financial picture. The evidence points to a wide Democratic margin, and nothing suggests a competitive contest. The main open question is the size of the victory rather than the winner.
